say:13:1621759011:1.text: After reading the novel and knowing the mirror could boost mana, I bet Girod just had to try it...

say:15:1621759013:1.text: Hold on! If Girod's been replaced, where is he now? I-I just hope he isn't stuck inside the mirror!

say:16:1621759014:1.text: ... Ah, I get it now! No wonder "Girod" was pushing us so hard to destroy the mirror!

say:17:1621759015:1.text: Leo, do you know what Seline's talking about?

say:18:1621759016:1.source_cn: 我从来跟不上她的思路，你又不是不知道。

say:22:1621759020:1.source_cn: 所以它坚持要毁掉古董镜，它要让真正的吉罗德跟着镜子一起...

say:23:1621759021:1.text: It still doesn't make sense. Why go through all that trouble to involve us when it could have just smashed the mirror? It had plenty of chances to do it as a store assistant.
say:23:1621759021:1.source_cn: 等一下，如果是这样的话，它直接毁掉镜子不是更简单？反正...

say:24:1621759022:1.text: And there would be no risk of exposing itself. Isn't that a smarter move?

say:25:1621759023:1.text: Because Girod is a poor student.
say:25:1621759023:1.source_cn: 因为它现在是“吉罗德”吧。经济不富裕、要拼命兼职打工的...

say:26:1621759024:1.text: First, "Girod" can't afford to buy the mirror. Second, if it smashed the mirror, there's no guarantee the store owner wouldn't notice. If it got caught, the owner would definitely demand compensation.

say:27:1621759025:1.text: So, it had no choice but to think of another way to get its hands on the mirror...

say:28:1621759026:1.text: I see! The whole thing was a scheme to force the store owner into giving us the mirror, so it could eventually destroy it!

say:30:1621759028:1.text: Ugh, I didn't see this coming at all... I trusted it completely!
